title: Assessing protein purity by SDS-PAGE with Coomassie staining
summary: Prepare reduced, heat-denatured samples, run them on a precast gel at constant 180 V alongside a ladder, and stain with Coomassie G250 to judge purity by band pattern. Community protocol on protocols.io (draft, no DOI).

steps.text: Dilute the purified protein to about 0.5 mg/mL (cell lysates about 20 mg/mL), after measuring concentration with a Bradford assay.
Mix sample with 4x LDS sample buffer and DTT, bringing the total to 50 uL.
Heat the mixture at 95 C for 5 minutes.
Rinse the wells of a precast 4-12% gel, mount it, and fill the buffer chambers with 1x running buffer.
Load a prestained ladder (10 uL) and samples (about 10 uL purified protein, 20 uL lysate), keeping under the well capacity.
Run at constant 180 V until the dye front reaches the bottom; this takes roughly 30-70 minutes depending on gel and buffer.
Wash the gel in warm water, stain with Coomassie G250 for about 30 minutes with gentle agitation, de-stain, and read the bands for contaminants.

equipment.name: Mini vertical gel system (source used a different brand)

safety: Concentrated HCl (used to make the stain) goes in a fume hood.
Never touch the tank while power is on; switch off before handling leaks.
